title: Agitavit's priority-4 rank comes from size and slot occupancy, not from any screen of its eHRM product
content:
Agitavit Solutions never went through v3 scoring. Its row was carried over from the tail of the v2 ranking, marked provisional, and its rank was recomputed mechanically from two inputs only: size and slot occupancy. Priority 4 is therefore a queue position rather than a judgement about the firm, and the flag says so explicitly by deferring to an OSS-portfolio screen that has not been run.

What the record does hold is the shape of the problem. The only platform associated with Agitavit is its own eHRM product, and its v2 verticals are HR software plus a broad remainder. A firm whose principal platform is software it wrote itself is a different conversation from an integrator with an open platform slot: the first has to be persuaded to change its own roadmap, the second only has to be persuaded to place a component in a client project.

The commercial consequence is that acting on the rank as if it were evidence risks spending outreach on a slot that is already filled by in-house IP. The cheap next step is the screen the flag asks for, not a call.
